thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Open Mixed As Investors Seek To Overcome Global Growth, Trade Concerns

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Open Mixed As Investors Seek To Overcome Global Growth, Trade Concerns
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer and Chris Matthews, MarketWatch
China's exports are weaker than expected
U.S. stocks traded mixed at the start of trade Monday, as investors struggled to weigh the importance of a still-healthy U.S. economy with evidence of slowing growth abroad and continued trade tensions.
Benchmarks
 fell 60 points or 0.3%, 24,334, while the S&P 500 rose less than a point. The Nasdaq Composite Index advanced 42 points to 7,012.
On Friday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/a-bruised-stock-market-looks-to-the-fed-for-relief-2018-12-08), the Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled 558.72 points, or 2.2%, to close at 24,388.95, the S&P 500 index retreated 2.3%, to 2,633.08, while the Nasdaq Composite Index slumped 3% to finish at 6,969.25.
That capped a week wherein all three major benchmarks saw their largest weekly percentage declines since March, and in which both the Dow and the S&P fell into negative territory for 2018.
Market drivers
Friday's healthy jobs data wasn't enough to offset growing concerns about the state of the global economy, and new data showing a sharp slowdown in Chinese export growth (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-export-growth-slows-sharply-in-november-2018-12-10) added to the worry pile.
Nevertheless, bulls have plenty of evidence to support the belief that the American economy can continue to grow at a healthy pace into next year and beyond, including survey data from manufacturers and service providers (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ism-service-index-registers-second-strongest-reading-in-13-years-2018-12-06) showing resilient demand and a healthy U.S. consumer.
Investors are increasingly focused on the Dec. 18-19 Federal Reserve meeting, where the central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates. Comments from Fed Chairman Jerome Powell will be in the spotlight, and if he strikes a more conciliatory tone, hinting at a slowing of future hikes, it could spark the highly anticipated Santa rally, bullish investors say (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/a-bruised-stock-market-looks-to-the-fed-for-relief-2018-12-08).
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/a-bruised-stock-market-looks-to-the-fed-for-relief-2018-12-08)But trade worries have also been getting in the way of traditional end-of-year gains. China's Vice Foreign Minister Le Yucheng summoned the U.S. ambassador on Sunday (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-12-10/china-calls-in-us-ambassador-over-huawei-affair/10598840) to insist the U.S. withdraw its arrest warrant on Huawei's chief financial officer Meng Wanzhou, who was detained on Dec. 1 in Canada.
Read:Huawei arrest creates concerns in Silicon Valley as well as abroad (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/huawei-arrest-creates-concerns-in-silicon-valley-as-well-as-abroad-2018-12-06)
Some are worried that the Huawei executive's arrest, news of which triggered sharp losses for Wall Street and global markets last week, will make it tough for China to follow through on trade concessions to the U.S. Investors are already dubious over how much progress was made between the two countries at the recent G-20 meeting.
Fears of an escalating trade conflict were also compounded by comments from U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer, who told CBS' Face the Nation on Sunday (https://www.cbsnews.com/news/transcript-amb-robert-lighthizer-on-face-the-nation-december-9-2018/) that he considers the 90-day moratorium from new tariffs granted to the Chinese a "hard deadline," and that the administration is not considering delaying an escalation of the trade conflict if the two sides can't agree to an armistice by March 1st.
Opinion:The stock market is overreacting because fears about the economy are overblown (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-stock-market-is-overreacting-because-fears-about-the-economy-are-overblown-2018-12-08)
British Prime Minister Theresa May reportedly will postpone a vote (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sterling-dives-to-fresh-18-month-low-as-brexit-vote-reportedly-cancelled-2018-12-10) on her plan for the U.K. to exit from the European Union, potentially adding another complication to the fraught Brexit process. Investors will also watch negotiations between Italy and the EU over Rome's planned budget deficit.
What are the analysts saying?
"The majority of the news last week [was] net positive," Tom Essaye, president of the Sevens Report, wrote in a Monday note to clients.
"There won't be 25% tariffs on Jan 1, and momentum toward a deal appears to be building, as the jobs report was solid but not too hot, while ISM Manufacturing PMIs were strong, and the Fed is shifting more and more dovish," he wrote.
"Hopes of fruitful trade negotiations have taken a beating since the optimism that was around a week ago when the Buenos Aires G-20 meeting prompted hope of a rally into the end of the year for equities," said Kit Juckes, global macro strategist at Société Générale, in a note. But he added that as Mondays are often an extension of what happened Friday, the rest of the week can't be judged too heavily on one session.
Stocks in focus
Shares of Tesla Inc. (TSLA)may be in focus after Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk appeared on "60 Minutes," (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-slams-sec-says-teslas-critics-have-been-unfair-and-outrageous-2018-12-09) defending himself and the company from what he referred to as "relentless criticism." Musk said he set and made a production target of 5,000 Model 3s a week and made the company itself profitable. Shares are up 1.5% Friday morning.
Apple Inc. (AAPL) stock is the Dow's biggest loser early Monday, down 1.6% after a key supplier, Japan Display Inc. said it was cutting production for crystal display panels for the iPhone XR.
Axovant Sciences Ltd. (AXON) stock is falling more than 30% early Monday, after the drugmaker announced (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/axovant-shares-slide-24-premarket-after-trial-of-treatment-for-sleep-disorder-fails-to-meet-main-goal-2018-12-10) that a trial of a treatment for REM sleep behavior disorder wasn't successful.
Shares of German chemical producer BASF SE(BAS.XE) are falling 4.4% Monday, after the firm warned that its profits would fall between 15% and 20% in 2018.
Aurora Cannabis Inc. (ACB.T) shares are in focus Monday after it said (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/aurora-cannabis-to-buy-mexican-partner-farmacias-magistrales-in-stock-deal-2018-12-10) that it has entered a letter of intent to buy Mexico's Farmacias Magistrales SA in a stock deal.
Shares of Linde Plc. (LIN.XE) are rising 2.5% Monday, after the multinational chemical company announced a $1 billion share repurchase program. Shares are up 2.5% in premarket trade.
What data are in focus?
The Labor Department said U.S. job openings rose to 7.08 million in October (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics), from 6.96 million a month earlier.
Other markets
Asian markets were under fresh pressure on Monday, with China's Shanghai Composite Index dropping 0.8% and the Nikkei 225 index down 2.1%. European markets were under pressure.
U.S. crude oil prices were lower, while gold and the U.S. dollar were largely flat.
